metaData.originalTitle: Hermes Agent：那个真的会记住昨天学过东西的开源 AI Agent
metaData.title: Hermes Agent: The Open-Source AI Agent That Actually Remembers What It Learned Yesterday
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core architecture of the open-source AI Agent Hermes, focusing on its closed-loop learning mechanism, four-tier memory system, and the distinction between Skills and Tools, along with deployment guidance and an honest assessment.
metaData.summary: Starting with the pain point of "AI Agents resetting every session," the article introduces Nous Research's open-source Hermes Agent. Its core innovation is "closed-loop learning": after successfully completing a task, the Agent encodes successful steps into a reusable Markdown Skill document via post-execution evaluation, enabling compounding knowledge growth. The article details Hermes' four-tier memory system (MEMORY.md, USER.md, session search, external memory plugins) and explains the key architectural distinction between Skills (autonomously written Markdown manuals) and Tools (deterministic Python functions). For deep research, Hermes uses a `think_tool` to enforce strategic pauses and parallel sub-agents for complex tasks. On security, it contrasts OpenClaw's supply chain risks, emphasizing that Hermes' internally generated Skills bypass external attack vectors. The article also provides a complete deployment guide and honestly assesses limitations such as local inference hardware requirements and the fragility of self-built Skills.

mainPoints.point: Hermes achieves compounding knowledge growth through a "closed-loop learning" mechanism.
mainPoints.explanation: After successfully completing a task, the Agent encodes successful steps into a reusable Markdown Skill document via post-execution evaluation. When encountering a similar task next time, it can directly reference this Skill, allowing the Agent to improve over time.

mainPoints.point: The architectural distinction between Skills and Tools is a core design of Hermes.
mainPoints.explanation: Tools are deterministic Python functions, while Skills are Markdown manuals that the Agent can autonomously write. Without modifying the source code, the Agent accumulates knowledge by writing Skills, keeping the tool layer stable and the knowledge layer continuously growing.

mainPoints.point: The four-tier memory system manages context hierarchically based on urgency.
mainPoints.explanation: Tier 1 (MEMORY.md) and Tier 2 (USER.md) use a frozen snapshot mode injected at session start, Tier 3 (session search) uses SQLite full-text search, and Tier 4 (external memory plugins) connects to a graph database, balancing information density with token cost.

mainPoints.point: The deep research function is achieved through forced strategic pauses and parallel sub-agents.
mainPoints.explanation: The Agent first calls `think_tool` to formulate a research plan, then delegates research topics to multiple parallel sub-agents, and finally calls `think_tool` again for synthesis, ensuring a structured and in-depth research process.

mainPoints.point: The design of internally generated Skills fundamentally mitigates external supply chain risks.
mainPoints.explanation: Unlike OpenClaw, which relies on public registries, Hermes' Skills are generated by the Agent within its own environment, bypassing malicious Skills and supply chain attacks. Combined with container isolation and dynamic credential rotation, this offers higher security.

keyQuotes: Hermes' core innovation can be summed up in one word: compounding.
Most AI Agents are in a 'reset every session' mode... Hermes breaks this pattern. It turns every successful operation into permanent, reusable knowledge.
The Agent gets smarter without touching its own source code. The deterministic tool layer remains stable and secure. The knowledge layer grows continuously.
